subject: Clarify SOC 2 scope across Hosted, Dedicated, and VPC (Acme Financial request)
messages:
From: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@acme.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: procure@acme.com, security@acme.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 Type II report + scope questions for our deployment

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for taking the call earlier. Acme is preparing our vendor risk review and need to confirm the scope of Redwood's SOC 2 Type II coverage. We're running a hybrid architecture: most traffic goes to Redwood Hosted endpoints, but we also use a Dedicated GPU pool for high-throughput inference (reserved capacity) and a VPC/private deployment for certain regulated workloads.

Could you confirm whether the current SOC 2 Type II (most recent period) covers:
- Hosted API endpoints (api.redwood.ai)
- Dedicated customer pools (reserved instances)
- Private VPC/private deployment (customer-managed network)

If any of those modes are out of scope, we need to understand the path for evidence (bridge letter, compensating controls) and whether you can provide a scoped bridge or attestation for the period Jan 1–Apr 30, 2027. Attaching our standard questionnaire and the initial request packet.

Attachments: Acme_SOC2_Request_0527.pdf (PDF questionnaire)

Appreciate a quick confirmation so we can finish procurement.

Regards,
Sarah Lopez
Senior Security Engineer
Acme Financial

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@acme.com>
Cc: procure@acme.com, security@acme.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II report + scope questions for our deployment

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear summary and the questionnaire. Short answer: our SOC 2 Type II report covers our hosted control plane and hosted inference endpoints for the audit period, but there are nuance items for Dedicated pools and Private/VPC deployments.

High level: 
- Hosted API: in-scope (covered by Redwood's report)
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools): typically in-scope when pooled capacity is operated within Redwood-managed infrastructure under our tenancy model; however, isolated single-tenant hardware and certain cross-tenant routing exceptions can require a scoped bridge.
- Private/VPC (customer-managed networking / on-prem): out-of-scope for controls that rely on the customer's network boundary and for certain physical/access controls — we can provide a bridge letter that maps which controls are not applicable and recommended compensating controls.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Can you attach a short topology diagram showing which workloads are served from Hosted vs Dedicated vs VPC? (A one-page PDF is fine.)
2) I will loop in our audits lead and our compliance SME to confirm the exact list of controls that require bridge language.

I'm attaching the topology deck we use internally to map hosting modes to control ownership.

Attachments: redwood_sow_topology_v1.pdf (topology + ownership mapping)

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Solutions & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Cc: procure@acme.com, security@acme.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: SOC 2 Type II report + scope questions for our deployment

Jonas / Karthik — FYI, Acme (procurement + infosec) asked whether our Type II covers hosted, dedicated pools, and their VPC private deployment for the period Jan–Apr 2027. Sarah attached their questionnaire.

Key asks: they want (1) confirmation of which hosting modes are explicitly covered by our report for that period; (2) if Dedicated is in-scope how we handle single-tenant isolation vs shared pooled capacity; (3) if Private/VPC is out-of-scope what the bridge language and recommended compensating controls look like.

My recommended response: confirm hosted covered, provide bullet list for dedicated exceptions (routing/cross-tenant exposure, burst/shared pools), and offer a draft bridge letter referencing the audit period. Can you review and supply final control mappings? Also tagging Jonas for final sign-off on the bridge letter text.

Quoted message below.

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: procure@acme.com, security@acme.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: SOC 2 Type II report + scope questions for our deployment

Kimberly — thanks for the clear framing. Confirming internally after a quick review with audit ops:

- Hosted API endpoints (api.redwood.ai) are in-scope for the Jan 1–Apr 30, 2027 Type II report. We will provide the Type II PDF for that period.
- Dedicated pools: in-scope when customers are on Redwood-managed reserved pools that do not have explicit single-tenant hardware exclusions. For customers using dedicated "single-tenant" blades or on-prem connectors that transfer control to the customer-managed environment, those specific control areas are not covered. We will annotate the relevant controls (primarily physical access, network segmentation, and certain change management controls) in the bridge letter.
- Private/VPC/on-prem: out-of-scope for controls dependent on customer network, physical site security, and customer-managed keys. We will prepare a bridge letter that lists the out-of-scope control numbers and suggested compensating controls Acme can assert (e.g., KMS attestation, private network firewall configs, quarterly audit evidence).

Action items:
1) Kimberly to share the final topology from Acme (one-pager).
2) Jonas to attach the Jan–Apr 2027 SOC 2 Type II PDF and a redlineable bridge letter by EOD tomorrow.
3) Karthik to confirm whether any dedicated-burst routing fallbacks during the period would change coverage (he will check routing logs for May).

We'll include the control mapping spreadsheet as an appendix to the bridge letter so Acme can cross-reference their questionnaire.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Audit Operations
Redwood Inference
